question.stem:
A Solutions Architect working for a startup is designing a High Performance Computing (HPC) application which is publicly accessible for their customers. The startup founders want to mitigate distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on their application.
Which of the following options are not suitable to be implemented in this scenario? (Select TWO.)
options: Use an Amazon CloudFront service for distributing both static and dynamic content.
Add multiple Elastic Fabric Adapters (EFA) to each EC2 instance to increase the network bandwidth.
Use Dedicated EC2 instances to ensure that each instance has the maximum performance possible.
Use AWS Shield and AWS WAF.
Use an Application Load Balancer with Auto Scaling groups for your EC2 instances. Prevent direct Internet traffic to your Amazon RDS database by deploying it to a new private subnet.
question.explanation: DDoS mitigation relies on absorbing and filtering traffic at the edge and scaling: CloudFront for static and dynamic content, Shield and WAF, and an ALB with Auto Scaling in front of a database in a private subnet (reducing the attack surface). Elastic Fabric Adapters only speed up node-to-node HPC/ML traffic and do nothing against DDoS, and Dedicated Instances only give hardware isolation for the instances, they add no DDoS protection. Those two are the options that are not suitable.

concept: DDoS mitigation: CloudFront + Shield + WAF + ALB/ASG + private subnets (EFA and Dedicated Instances don't help)
tests: Recognizing which measures mitigate DDoS (edge distribution, Shield/WAF, load balancing with scaling, reduced attack surface) and which are performance/isolation features that don't (EFA, Dedicated Instances). Note the question asks for what is NOT suitable.
expected: Not suitable: multiple EFAs (HPC network bandwidth) and Dedicated EC2 instances (hardware isolation). Suitable: CloudFront, Shield + WAF, ALB + Auto Scaling with RDS in a private subnet. Triggers: 'mitigate DDoS', 'not suitable' (inverted question).
why_not: Reading the question inverted: CloudFront, Shield/WAF and ALB + ASG with a private database are valid DDoS mitigations. EFA is a network interface for tightly-coupled HPC/ML and Dedicated Instances are for hardware isolation/licensing, neither mitigates DDoS.
